findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R4/p1/probe.py (HOME set to a temp dir): after appending to $HOME/.gitconfig only, L.git_control_digest(repo) and L.control_state(...) are unchanged (True True). (a) A [url "<fake.git>"] insteadOf=<origin> entry: driver-style push `[*GIT, -C, repo, push, origin, sha:refs/heads/main]` exits 0 and `git(repo, 'ls-remote', 'origin', ...)` returns the pushed sha, so integrate() would record INTEGRATED and reach COMPLETE, but the real origin main was never updated (printed: real origin main: False). (b) A global [filter "x"] smudge/clean plus a committed `.gitattributes` (a.py filter=x): blob in commit is 'DEFECT = True', the file in the driver's add_worktree() checkout reads 'DEFECT = False', and worktree_changes() reports the checkout clean, so the reviewer reads and the gates test content that is not the candidate tree, and the integrity check passes. Workers inherit HOME (lifecycle_providers.py:131) and can write ~/.gitconfig with plain shell (the Bash(git config*) prefix denial does not cover `cat >> ~/.gitconfig`). Same class as R1-04/R3-01 (worker-written config steering driver git commands), outside the monitored set.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the effective global/system config files (git config --show-origin --list --global/--system, or GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL / XDG paths) and the default core.attributesFile ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/attributes) in control_state/git_control_digest, or run driver git with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM isolation (plus a separately pinned credential/push configuration). Verify pushes against the remote URL recorded at PLAN (e.g. `git remote get-url` resolved without insteadOf, bound in the chain). Add regression tests for the insteadOf and smudge-filter cases.
findings.title: Git control-state tamper check covers only the repository config; worker-written user-level git config (~/.gitconfig) silently redirects the driver's push and its push verification, and smudge filters make reviewer/gate checkouts differ from the candidate commit

findings.evidence: effective_verdict({'verdict':'ACCEPT','findings':[{'id':'R1-01','severity':'HIGH','title':123}]}) -> REJECT, then _fingerprint() raises AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'lower' (assess_progress/count_attempts). run() does not catch it; the stage stays AUDITING with no receipt. Fail-safe (never ACCEPT), but the round is lost and the next run re-reviews.
findings.suggested_fix: Coerce title/id/files with str() in _fingerprint/count_attempts, or reject non-string fields in result_problem as unparseable.
findings.title: A REJECT result with a non-string finding title crashes the driver (uncaught AttributeError) instead of routing to repair
